ehr:terminal:001.title: Final Inpatient Status and Discharge Disposition
ehr:terminal:001.content: During hospitalization, the total thyroidectomy, regional lymph node management, and postoperative rehabilitation documented in the source record were completed. The discharge diagnosis was malignant thyroid tumor, the treatment outcome was cured, and the discharge disposition was discharge per medical advice.

img:008.title: Color Doppler ultrasound
img:008.content:
Solid nodules near the isthmus and in the posterolateral middle portion of the left thyroid lobe: provisionally C-TIRADS category 4C (3-4 points); FNA has been performed at an outside hospital, revised to C-TIRADS category 6. Solid nodules in the anterolateral lower pole and central anterior aspect of the mid-upper pole of the right thyroid lobe: provisionally C-TIRADS category 4B (2 points); FNA is recommended. Bilateral thyroid nodules, provisionally C-TIRADS category 3; please correlate clinically. Abnormal lymph node in left cervical level III: mildly suspicious for metastatic lymph node; FNA is recommended. (Explanation: C-TIRADS categories 1-2, probability of malignancy 0%; C-TIRADS category 3, probability of malignancy <2%; C-TIRADS category 4A, probability of malignancy 2-10%; C-TIRADS category 4B, probability of malignancy 10-50%; C-TIRADS category 4C, probability of malignancy 50-90%; C-TIRADS category 5, probability of malignancy >90%; C-TIRADS category 6, biopsy-proven malignant nodule. Revised C-TIRADS refers to the category after modification of the nodule risk level based on the physician's experience or medical history. Reference: Endocrine, 2120, 256-279)
Thyroid: Both thyroid lobes are normal in contour, with smooth capsules, homogeneous internal echogenicity, and multiple variably sized predominantly cystic and predominantly solid nodules within the parenchyma. The largest on the left measures 9.9 ×6.0 mm, and the largest on the right measures 5.4× 2.5mm. Elastography shows that the above nodules are soft to intermediate, with elasticity scores of 2-3 points (using a 5-point scoring method). CFI shows normal blood supply in the thyroid parenchyma. Within the left thyroid lobe near the isthmus, there is a mass with a transverse diameter of 8.3mm, an anteroposterior diameter of 10.1mm, and a craniocaudal diameter of 10.5mm. It is closely abutting the capsule, grows in a vertical orientation (1 point), has irregular margins (1 point), has a solid internal structure (1 point), and is hypoechoic (0 point). No obvious punctate hyperechoic foci are seen. CFI shows predominantly peripheral blood supply in the mass, with sparse vascularity. Elastography shows that the nodule is hard, with an elasticity score of 4 points (using a 5-point scoring method). In the posterolateral middle portion of the left thyroid lobe, there is a mass with a transverse diameter of 7.9mm, an anteroposterior diameter of 10.0mm, and a craniocaudal diameter of 10.1mm. It is closely abutting the capsule, grows in a vertical orientation (1 point), has irregular margins (1 point), has a solid internal structure (1 point), and is hypoechoic (0 point). No obvious punctate hyperechoic foci are seen. CFI shows predominantly peripheral blood supply in the mass, with sparse vascularity. Elastography shows that the nodule is hard, with an elasticity score of 4 points (using a 5-point scoring method). In the anterolateral lower pole of the right thyroid lobe, there is a mass with a transverse diameter of 3.9mm, an anteroposterior diameter of 4.1mm, and a craniocaudal diameter of 4.8mm. It is 1.2mm from the anterior capsule, grows in a vertical orientation (1 point), has smooth margins (0 point), has a solid internal structure (1 point), and is hypoechoic (0 point). No obvious punctate hyperechoic foci are seen. CFI shows predominantly peripheral blood supply in the mass, with sparse vascularity. Elastography shows that the nodule is hard, with an elasticity score of 4 points (using a 5-point scoring method). In the central anterior aspect of the mid-upper pole of the right thyroid lobe, there is a mass with a transverse diameter of 2.1mm, an anteroposterior diameter of 2.4mm, and a craniocaudal diameter of 1.9mm. It is closely abutting the anterior capsule, grows in a vertical orientation (1 point), has smooth margins (0 point), has a solid internal structure (1 point), and is hypoechoic (0 point). No obvious punctate hyperechoic foci are seen. CFI shows predominantly peripheral blood supply in the mass, with sparse vascularity. Elastography shows that the nodule is hard, with an elasticity score of 4 points (using a 5-point scoring method). One lymph node is seen in left cervical level III, measuring approximately 10.8×3.6mm. The lymphatic hilum is not seen. CDFI: a small amount of blood-flow signal is seen. No obvious abnormally enlarged lymph nodes are seen in the right neck. Three-dimensional ultrasonography shows no obvious abnormal distribution in the gland or soft tissues. Three-dimensional color and power Doppler ultrasonography shows no large, tortuous vessels with a radial distribution in either the sagittal or coronal plane.

The largest on the left measures 9.9 ×6.0 mm, and the largest on the right measures 5.4× 2.5mm. Elastography shows that the above nodules are soft to intermediate, with elasticity scores of 2-3 points (a 5-point scoring system). CFI shows normal blood supply to the thyroid parenchyma. It abuts the capsule, grows in a taller-than-wide orientation (1 points), has irregular margins (1 points), has a solid internal structure (1 points), and is hypoechoic (0 points). No obvious punctate echogenic foci are seen. CFI shows predominantly peripheral blood flow in the mass, with sparse vascularity. Elastography shows that the nodule is hard, with an elasticity score of 4 points (a 5-point scoring system). It abuts the capsule, grows in a taller-than-wide orientation (1 points), has irregular margins (1 points), has a solid internal structure (1 points), and is hypoechoic (0 points). No obvious punctate echogenic foci are seen. CFI shows predominantly peripheral blood flow in the mass, with sparse vascularity. Elastography shows that the nodule is hard, with an elasticity score of 4 points (a 5-point scoring system). In the anterolateral aspect of the lower pole of the right thyroid lobe, there is a mass with a transverse diameter of 3.9mm, an anteroposterior diameter of 4.1mm, and a craniocaudal diameter of 4.8mm. It is 1.2mm from the anterior capsule, grows in a taller-than-wide orientation (1 points), has smooth margins (0 points), has a solid internal structure (1 points), and is hypoechoic (0 points). No obvious punctate echogenic foci are seen. CFI shows predominantly peripheral blood flow in the mass, with sparse vascularity. Elastography shows that the nodule is hard, with an elasticity score of 4 points (a 5-point scoring system). In the central anterior aspect of the mid-upper pole of the right thyroid lobe, there is a mass with a transverse diameter of 2.1mm, an anteroposterior diameter of 2.4mm, and a craniocaudal diameter of 1.9mm. It abuts the anterior capsule, grows in a taller-than-wide orientation (1 points), has smooth margins (0 points), has a solid internal structure (1 points), and is hypoechoic (0 points). Left cervical lymph nodes: level VI, normal appearance; level II, normal appearance; level III, mildly suspicious, located lateral to the jugular vein, measuring approximately 10.8×3.6mm, and slightly plump in morphology; level IV, normal appearance; level V, normal appearance. Right cervical lymph nodes: level VI, normal appearance; level II, normal appearance; level III, normal appearance; level IV, normal appearance; level V, normal appearance. Flow velocities in the bilateral carotid arteries, jugular veins, superior thyroid arteries, and inferior thyroid arteries are essentially normal, without obvious signs of compression or invasion. Three-dimensional ultrasonography shows no obvious abnormal distribution pattern in the glands or soft tissues. Three-dimensional color and power Doppler ultrasonography shows no large, tortuous vessels with a radial distribution on either sagittal or coronal planes. The bilateral submandibular glands are essentially normal in shape and size, with smooth capsules, poorly defined boundaries with the surrounding tissues, normal and homogeneously distributed parenchymal echogenicity, and mildly increased blood supply on CFI. No obvious dilatation of the bilateral submandibular gland ducts is seen.

img:010.title: Fine-needle aspiration
img:010.content:
Solid nodule at the middle-lower pole of the right thyroid lobe: provisionally classified as C-TIRADS category 4B. Lymph node in left cervical level III. Ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration was performed 5 time(s) on each of the above nodule and lymph node; await cytological results. (Note: ① If ultrasound suggests that the nodule is suspicious for malignancy, or is C-TIRADS category 4B, 4C, or 5, while cytology is benign, repeat aspiration is recommended; ② If cytology indicates "a small number of thyroid epithelial cells and blood cells are seen on the smear," repeat aspiration is also recommended.) (Explanation: C-TIRADS categories 1-2, probability of malignancy 0%; C-TIRADS category 3, probability of malignancy <2%; C-TIRADS category 4A, probability of malignancy 2-10%; C-TIRADS category 4B, probability of malignancy 10-50%; C-TIRADS category 4C, probability of malignancy 50-90%; C-TIRADS category 5, probability of malignancy >90%; C-TIRADS category 6, biopsy-proven malignant nodule. Modified C-TIRADS refers to classification after modification of the nodule's risk of malignancy based on the physician's experience or medical history. Reference: Endocrine, 2120, 256-279)
A nodule measuring approximately 3.6 × 4.3 × 5.0mm is seen in the central ventral portion of the middle-lower pole of the right thyroid lobe. It grows in a vertical orientation (1 point[s]), has smooth and regular margins (0 point[s]), and no halo is seen. Its internal structure is solid (1 point[s]) and hypoechoic (0 point[s]); no obvious punctate hyperechoic foci are seen. CFI shows peripheral vascularity in the nodule, with sparse blood flow. Elastography shows that the nodule is hard, with an elasticity score of 4 point(s) (5-point scoring method). Aspiration record: The patient was placed in the supine position with the neck fully exposed. Routine disinfection was performed. A 7-gauge fine aspiration needle was used, and aspiration was performed under ultrasound guidance. The aspirated specimen was satisfactory, and 1 smear(s) were prepared. A specimen for multigene testing was retained. No bleeding occurred after local compression of the aspiration site. Monitor the aspiration site after the procedure. Seek prompt medical attention in the event of severe symptoms such as bleeding, neck swelling, or difficulty breathing. A lymph node measuring approximately 10.1 × 3.9 × 12.8 mm is seen in left cervical level III. No fusion between lymph nodes is seen. The capsule is smooth and regular, with clear demarcation from the surrounding soft tissue. The lymph node is oval, and its hilum is eccentric. The interior of the lymph node is hypoechoic (compared with the adjacent muscle), with relatively uniform distribution. No obvious calcific hyperechoic foci or liquefactive anechoic areas are seen. CFI demonstrates hilar vessels in the lymph node, with sparse blood flow. Elastography shows the lymph node hardness to be hard (elasticity score: 3 point[s], 4-point scoring method). Aspiration record: The patient was placed in the supine position with the neck fully exposed. Routine disinfection was performed. A 7-gauge fine aspiration needle was used, and aspiration was performed under ultrasound guidance. The aspirated specimen was satisfactory, and 1 smear(s) were prepared. A specimen for multigene testing was retained. No bleeding occurred after local compression of the aspiration site. Monitor the aspiration site after the procedure. Seek prompt medical attention in the event of severe symptoms such as bleeding or swelling at the aspiration site.

path:006.title: Cytopathology
path:006.content: Follicular epithelial cells arranged in sheets and papillary formations are seen. Some cells are crowded, with enlarged nuclei; nuclear grooves and intranuclear inclusions are visible in occasional cells, consistent with papillary thyroid carcinoma. Note: Bethesda reporting category VI

path:007.title: Cytopathology
path:007.content: Lymphocytes are seen; no evidence of malignancy is seen.
